segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast, we have real conversations in easy English

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.text: And I'm Beth. You can find a video version of this podcast

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Beth, how are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm good, Neil, how are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Very well, thank you.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What are we talking about today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Today we are talking about housemates.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, housemates.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The people that you share a house with who aren't your family.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Maybe they're your friends or even strangers who just need somewhere to live.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Exactly. And it's quite common in the UK to live with housemates when you're younger.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Have you ever lived with housemates?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, of course. I had house or flatmates when I was a student.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And then after I was a student in my first jobs and before I got married.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That's exactly the same as me.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So when I went to university I moved in with five people And we all had a separate room and a separate bathroom but yeah they were my flatmates for my first year of university but in my second year then I moved into a house

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and we all shared a bathroom and they were my housemates because we were in a house.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Did you enjoy having housemates?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think it really depends on the people that you live with I have had some bad housemates

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: bad because they weren't tidy didn't clean there were dishes in the kitchen that were dirty and

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: not cleaned for a long time but I've also had some really nice housemates as well do you enjoy

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: living with housemates? Or did you enjoy living with housemates?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think, as you said, it really

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: depends on the person. So you mentioned people being messy and that kind of thing. Also, noisy

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: people are difficult. But some of my best friends now have been my housemates in the past. So I think

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: you can really get to know people very well

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and you can also meet some people

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: who you never want to see again in your life

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That true So Neil what do you think is the best kind of personality the best kind of person to

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: live with?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: They have to be easygoing.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What does that mean?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Somebody who is easygoing is relaxed and they don't get too upset or angry over little

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: things. And they're quite easy to live with. And there's the clue, easygoing.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think something else important about living with other people or renting somewhere, so

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: paying monthly, is having a good landlord. Very important.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So who is a landlord? What is a landlord?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So the landlord is, or landlady, is the person that owns the house or flat that you're in and you pay them rent.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So you pay them a monthly amount, but you might live there for a year or two years or three years, but you don't own the place.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It's the landlord that owns the place.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, and a good landlord can make a big difference.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Neil, are you easy to live with?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: should we be flatmates

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I don't know

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but I think

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I have made some good friends when I been a housemate so they think that I was a good housemate Okay How about you

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, I think I'm easy to live with.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But I like to sing a lot.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So maybe people would tell me to be quiet.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Although no one's ever told me to be quiet,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but maybe they wanted me to and just didn't say.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the vocabulary we've heard in this podcast, starting with housemate.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A housemate is someone you live with who probably isn't part of your family.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We also hear flatmate.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we heard easygoing, which means relaxed and not easily upset.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Flatmates or housemates often rent a property and that means they don't own it,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: They pay money to the person who does own it.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And the person who owns the house or flat is the landlord.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That's who you pay every month and they own the property.
